title: Slow Network & DNS Resolution Failures
prerequisites: Access to Command Prompt or Terminal
diagnostic_questions: Is the slowness on all websites or specific ones?
Are you connected via Wi-Fi or Ethernet cable?
Has this been happening since a specific time?
Are other people near you experiencing the same issue?

resolution_steps.action: Let's flush your DNS cache to clear any stale entries. Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: ipconfig /flushdns
resolution_steps.checkpoint: Did you see 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache'?

resolution_steps.action: Release and renew your IP address. In the same Command Prompt, run: ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew
resolution_steps.checkpoint: Did you get a new IP address? (It should start with 10.x or 192.168.x)

resolution_steps.action: Try loading a website now. Open your browser and go to google.com.
resolution_steps.checkpoint: Is the website loading faster now?

resolution_steps.action: If the issue persists, try switching to a different DNS server temporarily. Open Network Settings → Change adapter options → right-click your connection → Properties → IPv4 → set DNS to 8.8.8.8 (primary) and 8.8.4.4 (secondary).
resolution_steps.checkpoint: Did switching DNS servers resolve the slowness?

escalation_criteria: If DNS changes don't help, or if the issue affects multiple users on the same floor/site
